title: UrgentAlert: a danger-class record notifies immediately
action: Close Plan Phase 2 (per c80debd7 'danger-class UrgentAlerts notify immediately' and the plan's Phase-2 row 'UrgentAlert immediate path'). Add a third mailbox kind `urgent` beside intervention|escalation in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/supervisor.rs, taking the SAME fields and the SAME validation seam (--target-session, --point-key, --question, one line, at most two sentences, control-token/secret refusal). Two differences only: (1) the point-key frequency cap does NOT refuse an urgent row — a danger-class alert is never suppressed by an earlier record on the same point; (2) on a successful write the verb fires exactly ONE best-effort desktop notification, immediately, in-process. Transport: `notify-send` is the cheapest real one on this machine (/usr/bin/notify-send) — build the command behind an injectable seam (a function returning the notifier argv, so tests assert the argv without spawning anything), spawn it detached and IGNORE every failure: a missing or failing notifier must never fail the record, never panic, never block. Honor an opt-out: read `supervisor.notify` from .bee/config.json through the existing config read path, defaulting to enabled, and skip the spawn when it is false. The urgent row is still an ordinary mailbox row: `pending` lists it and the sup-6 turn-boundary hook delivers it with the urgent prefix, so reuse delivery_line rather than adding a second renderer. Tests in the same tests module: an urgent record is accepted on a point that already carries an intervention (no cap); the notifier argv carries the target session and the question text; notify disabled in config builds no argv; a notifier that cannot run still leaves the row written and returns success; pending and mark-delivered treat urgent exactly like the other two kinds. Regen deferred to the wave barrier.
